items.title: Branford Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewee discusses John Coltrane's work with Ornette Coleman's band (which included Ed Blackwell) but does not mention any personal interaction, collaboration, or direct relationship with Ed Blackwell himself.

ctx.x: I think the ultimate goal is to get there without a system. I think that if Trane could have got there without a system, he would have done that. As a matter of fact, there’s a guy that nobody knows named Cuthbert Simpkins. So you know about Doc. Alright. Coltrane dies. He is a doctor living in Shreveport, Louisiana. Coltrane dies and he gets in his car and he drives to New York City and walks around with a tape recorder and just starts talking to musicians. “Tell me about Trane. Tell me about Trane.” Because he…

Its Ornette Colman’s band. Alright? The fact that he does a record with this band, playing Ornette’s music proves beyond a shadow of doubt that Trane was sick of the shit he was playing. And he had to find a way out of the system that he had created. Because there are other guys who are from that time and they feel comfortable playing in their system
